interactions.summary: Jiang runs a classroom experiment in which Francois turns around almost immediately when Edward silently looks at him, then uses the result to argue for morphic fields, soul-level connection, and openness to anomalous phenomena.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led experiment with brief student responses.

interactions.summary: A student resumes reading Canto 18 as the class returns from the experiment to the poem.

speaker_notes.note: The overlapping class response is noisy, but it mainly affirms surprise and suggests the group may have become more synchronized after many days together.

claims.claim: Jiang treats the rapid turnaround in the classroom demo as evidence that standard neuroscience cannot explain the effect while morphic-field theory can.
Jiang says souls are essentially morphic fields, which is why one person's act of looking can trigger another's response at a soul level.
Jiang extends this framework to say telepathy and even telekinesis become possible to some degree if people project outward through fields across dimensions.
Jiang uses the experiment rhetorically to argue that modern prejudices about how the world works prematurely close the mind to interesting possibilities.

signature_moments.moment: A tiny classroom stunt becomes an argument that souls project through fields and can feel each other's attention.
signature_moments.source_phrase: our souls are essentially these morphic fields
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is one of the lecture's strangest and most source-specific leaps from anecdote to metaphysics.

signature_moments.moment: Closed-mindedness is portrayed as the real obstacle, not lack of interesting evidence.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we close our minds to it
signature_moments.why_it_matters: Jiang uses the experiment less as proof than as a rebuke to default materialist dismissal.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang uses the term for soul-like fields that project outward, connect people across dimensions, and can explain rapid interpersonal response.

chronology_notes.note: This packet records a June 26 classroom experiment Jiang explicitly turns into a metaphysical claim about morphic fields and souls before returning to the text.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang's appeal to Sheldrake and anomalous phenomena is presented affirmatively here, but the packet does not supply a more formal argument beyond the live classroom demonstration.
